effect: The final picture shows some absorbed nutrients crossing toward liver cells while others remain in blood, and identifies sinusoids as broad capillary channels. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The distinction between nutrients entering cells and continuing in blood is useful, though their subsequent processing remains unexplained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the portal vessel was most worthwhile: the two-capillary-bed picture explains why the liver encounters intestinal blood before it reaches the wider circulation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the portal vessel into the digestive tube was straightforward but added little explanation on its own.

surprise.text: The liver receives a separate arterial input as well as portal blood; the completed route makes those inputs distinct from the bile ducts.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the later fittings were prescribed by the only available combinations rather than requiring a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue: tracing nutrients into liver cells raises a useful question about what the liver does with them next. The compatible-option menu made the route easy to follow, though not a discovery of compatibility.
